topic: The Power of Combination: Mastering Product and Chain Rules
target_audience: First-year university students or advanced high school calculus students

sections.title: Foundation: Derivative as a Rate of Change
sections.content: Briefly revisit the derivative as the instantaneous slope of a tangent line. Introduce the prerequisite: basic power rules and trigonometric derivatives. Establish the challenge: How do we differentiate functions that are multiplied together or nested inside one another?
sections.example: Visualizing a character, 'Calc-Bot', moving along a simple curve y = x^2, where the slope represents his instantaneous velocity.

sections.title: The Product Rule: Growing Areas
sections.content: Explain that the derivative of a product is NOT the product of the derivatives. Use a geometric approach: represent f(x) * g(x) as the area of a rectangle. As x increases, both the width (f) and height (g) grow. The total change in area is the sum of the growth of the two sides.
sections.example: Imagine a rectangular digital garden where width u(x) = x and height v(x) = sin(x). To find the rate of change of the area, we use the formula: d/dx(uv) = u'v + uv'.

sections.title: The Chain Rule: Linked Gears
sections.content: Introduce composite functions f(g(x)). Use the 'Gears' metaphor: if Gear A turns 3 times faster than Gear B, and Gear B turns 2 times faster than Gear C, Gear A turns 3 * 2 = 6 times faster than Gear C. This leads to the formula: dy/dx = (dy/du) * (du/dx).
sections.example: A 'Nested Doll' visual: An outer function (the big doll) contains an inner function (the small doll). To find the change, you must differentiate the big doll while keeping the small one inside, then multiply by the derivative of the small doll.

sections.title: The Synergy: Combining Both Rules
sections.content: Demonstrate a complex scenario where a product contains a composite function. This requires applying the Product Rule first, then using the Chain Rule during the differentiation of the individual terms. Emphasize tracking each 'layer' of the calculation.
sections.example: Calc-Bot is flying a drone. The altitude is h(x) = x^2 * sin(3x). Here, x^2 and sin(3x) are multiplied (Product Rule), but sin(3x) is nested (Chain Rule). The visual shows the calculation branches splitting and then recombining.

sections.title: Interactive Summary & Visual Recap
sections.content: A high-speed visual summary of the two formulas. Contrast them side-by-side: Product Rule = 'Addition of growth components'; Chain Rule = 'Multiplication of rates'. Provide a final mnemonic to help students remember the order of operations.
sections.example: A 30-second animation of the 'Rectangle' and the 'Gears' merging into a single master equation sheet, highlighting the key derivative symbols in bright neon colors.
